text:
The stock fell 14.61% over two weeks, with a sharp $37.84 drop on November 4th alone—the day after the midterm election results. News that day highlighted Democratic control of Congress, which typically favors renewable energy investment over traditional oil refining, creating near-term uncertainty about the regulatory environment for refiners like this one. The modest decline today (-0.13%) suggests the stock is stabilizing after that initial shock.

The underlying refining fundamentals remain relatively solid: refineries are running at 94.5% capacity and US oil is trading at $99.64 per barrel, indicating steady demand. However, the election outcome appears to have shifted investor sentiment about the longer-term policy direction for fossil fuel infrastructure, which is why the stock retreated sharply even as day-to-day operations remain healthy.
